What Is Flatbed Recovery?
Flatbed recovery uses a recovery vehicle with a flat loading platform. Instead of travelling on its own wheels, the vehicle is loaded onto the platform and transported to the required destination.
This method can be useful when a vehicle:
Will not start
Cannot move under its own power
Has accident damage
Has damaged wheels or tyres
Has a serious mechanical fault
Should not be driven
Needs transporting to a garage
Needs moving from one location to another

The appropriate recovery method depends on the vehicle, its condition, location and access. When you contact A.A.D Transport & Recovery, explain what has happened so the recovery requirements can be discussed before transportation is arranged.
When Do You Need Flatbed Recovery?

Not every breakdown requires a flatbed recovery vehicle. Some vehicles may be suitable for roadside assistance or another recovery method. However, flatbed transportation can be useful when a vehicle cannot safely be driven.
Non-Running Vehicles

If your vehicle will not start because of an engine, electrical or mechanical problem, it may need to be transported to a garage. Flatbed recovery provides a way to move the vehicle without requiring it to drive during the journey.
Accident-Damaged Vehicles
After an accident, a vehicle may have damage to its wheels, steering, suspension or bodywork. Even if the engine starts, the vehicle may not be safe to drive.
Suitable recovery can transport the vehicle to a garage, body shop or another agreed destination.
Serious Mechanical Faults

Major engine, transmission, steering or suspension faults can make continued driving unsuitable. Recovering the vehicle instead can help you avoid attempting to drive a vehicle that may not be safe to operate.

Severely damaged wheels or tyres can prevent normal driving. Depending on the vehicle and location, flatbed transportation may be an appropriate recovery option.

blocks.text: Wheel-Lift Recovery Birmingham – 24/7 Vehicle Towing

When a vehicle needs to be moved but cannot safely continue driving, wheel-lift recovery in Birmingham can provide a practical way to tow it. A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides vehicle recovery and transportation across Birmingham and the surrounding West Midlands.

Wheel-lift recovery uses a specialized lifting mechanism to raise the vehicle's wheels from the road while the recovery vehicle moves it. It can be useful for certain breakdowns, non-running vehicles and situations where a vehicle needs to be moved a short or longer distance.
For recovery assistance, call 07771 004242 and provide your location and vehicle details.
What Is Wheel-Lift Recovery?
A wheel-lift recovery system is designed to lift one end of a vehicle off the ground so it can be towed by a recovery vehicle.

Unlike a flatbed truck, where the complete vehicle is loaded onto a platform, wheel-lift recovery supports and lifts the vehicle by its wheels. The appropriate recovery method depends on the vehicle, its condition, location and the distance it needs to be transported.
This makes wheel-lift recovery a useful option for certain vehicles that need towing after a breakdown or when they cannot be driven.
When Is Wheel-Lift Recovery Used?
Wheel-lift recovery can be suitable in several situations where a vehicle needs to be moved but driving it is not practical.
Breakdown Recovery
If your vehicle has stopped working and cannot continue its journey, wheel-lift towing may provide a suitable recovery option depending on the vehicle's condition.
Non-Running Vehicles
A vehicle that will not start may still need to be moved from a roadside location to a garage or another destination.
Vehicle Relocation
Sometimes a vehicle simply needs to be moved from one location to another. Wheel-lift equipment can be useful where the vehicle can be safely secured for towing.
Roadside Recovery
If your vehicle has become immobilised on a local Birmingham road, professional recovery can help move it to a suitable location.
Garage Transportation
A vehicle that cannot safely drive to a garage can be recovered and transported for inspection or repairs.
How Does Wheel-Lift Recovery Work?
The exact recovery process depends on the vehicle and its condition, but the general process involves several stages.
1. Vehicle Assessment
The recovery operator considers the vehicle's condition, location and the reason it needs to be moved.
2. Positioning the Recovery Vehicle
The recovery vehicle is positioned safely so the wheel-lift equipment can be used.
3. Connecting the Wheel-Lift Equipment
The equipment is attached to the appropriate part of the vehicle according to the recovery requirements.
4. Lifting the Vehicle
The selected wheels are raised from the road and the vehicle is secured for transportation.
5. Vehicle Transportation
The vehicle is then moved carefully to the agreed destination.
The recovery method can vary depending on the vehicle type, drivetrain, condition and circumstances. If wheel-lift towing is not appropriate, another recovery method may be recommended.
Wheel-Lift vs Flatbed Recovery
Both wheel-lift and flatbed recovery can transport vehicles, but they work differently.
Wheel-Lift Recovery
Flatbed Recovery
Lifts part of the vehicle
Loads the complete vehicle onto a platform
Useful for suitable towing situations
Useful where all wheels need to be off the road
Can be practical for certain breakdowns
Often suitable for heavily damaged or specialist vehicles
Vehicle remains partly on the road
Vehicle travels fully on the recovery platform
Recovery suitability depends on vehicle type
Suitable for many different vehicle types
The right option depends on the condition and type of vehicle. If you are unsure which recovery method is suitable, provide the recovery team with your vehicle details when you call.
Is Wheel-Lift Recovery Suitable for Every Vehicle?
No. Wheel-lift recovery is not automatically suitable for every vehicle.
Factors such as the vehicle's drivetrain, steering, wheel condition, suspension, damage and overall condition can affect the appropriate recovery method.
For example, a vehicle with significant wheel or suspension damage may require a different method of recovery. Similarly, some vehicles may be better transported using a flatbed.

Before attempting anything, make sure your vehicle is in a safe position.
If you are stuck somewhere unsafe or close to moving traffic:

Common Signs of a Flat Car Battery

The Engine Does Not Start
You turn the key or press the start button but the engine does not crank normally.
Clicking Sound
You may hear repeated clicking when attempting to start the vehicle.
Dim Dashboard Lights
Dashboard lights may appear weaker than usual or switch off when you try to start the engine.
Electrical Equipment Stops Working
The radio, interior lights or other electrical systems may not work correctly.
Vehicle Has Been Left Unused
A vehicle that has not been driven for a long period may have a battery that has lost its charge.
Lights Were Left On
Leaving headlights, interior lights or another electrical system running can drain the battery.
These symptoms can have other causes as well, so a flat battery should not automatically be assumed to be the only problem.

Why Is My Car Battery Flat?
There are several reasons a vehicle battery may lose its charge.
Lights Left On
Headlights, interior lights or other electrical equipment can drain a battery if left running.
Vehicle Not Used for a Long Period
A vehicle that remains parked for an extended period may gradually lose battery charge.
Cold Weather
Low temperatures can affect battery performance, particularly when a battery is already weak.
Battery Age
Car batteries do not last indefinitely. An ageing battery may gradually become less reliable.
Electrical Fault
An electrical problem can sometimes cause unusual battery drain.
Charging System Problem
If the alternator or another part of the charging system is not working correctly, the battery may not receive the charge it needs while driving.

What Should You Do If You Have a Flat Tyre?
If you notice a puncture or sudden loss of tyre pressure while driving, the first priority is getting yourself and other passengers somewhere safe.
If it is safe to do so:
Slow down gradually
Avoid sudden steering or braking
Move to a safe location away from moving traffic
Switch on your hazard lights
Keep passengers away from the road
Do not continue driving on a severely damaged tyre
Contact roadside assistance if the vehicle cannot safely continue
If you are stopped in a dangerous position or there is an immediate risk to people, contact the emergency services first.
Common Causes of a Flat Tyre
A flat tyre can happen for different reasons. Some common causes include:
Puncture
A nail, screw, glass or another sharp object can penetrate the tyre and cause air to escape.
Damaged Sidewall
Impact with a kerb, pothole or another object can damage the tyre sidewall.
Loss of Air Pressure
A tyre may gradually lose pressure because of a slow puncture, valve issue or other problem.
Pothole Damage
A significant pothole can damage a tyre or wheel and may result in a sudden loss of pressure.
Worn Tyre
A heavily worn tyre may be more vulnerable to damage and may no longer provide safe road contact.
Valve Problem
A damaged or faulty valve can also contribute to loss of tyre pressure.
The exact cause is not always obvious from the roadside, so avoid assuming that simply adding air has solved the problem if the tyre continues to lose pressure.
Flat Tyre Assistance in Birmingham

Some punctures may be repairable, while other tyre damage may make the tyre unsuitable for further use. Sidewall damage, severe impact damage or a badly damaged tyre may require a replacement tyre or vehicle recovery rather than a simple repair.
For this reason, do not continue driving simply because the vehicle still appears to move.
If you are unsure about the condition of your tyre, stop in a safe location and seek appropriate assistance.
Can You Drive on a Flat Tyre?
Driving on a completely flat tyre is generally not advisable because it can cause further damage to the tyre and potentially the wheel.
Continuing to drive can also affect the vehicle's handling and braking.
If your tyre has lost significant pressure:
Slow down safely.
Avoid sudden movements.
Stop somewhere safe.

A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides roadside recovery support for different vehicle problems across Birmingham.

Breakdown Assistance
If your vehicle breaks down and cannot continue normally, contact us with your location and details of the problem. We can discuss the appropriate roadside recovery option.
Flat Battery Assistance

Fuel Delivery

Running out of fuel can bring a journey to an unexpected stop. A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides fuel delivery support by bringing the appropriate fuel to the roadside to help you continue your journey where possible.

What Should You Do When Your Car Breaks Down?
If your vehicle develops a problem while driving, your first priority should be safety.
Where possible:
Move the vehicle to a safe location away from moving traffic.
Switch on your hazard warning lights.
Keep yourself and passengers away from dangerous traffic areas.
Do not attempt repairs if you are in an unsafe position.
Contact roadside assistance and explain the problem.
Provide your exact location so help can be arranged.
If you are on a motorway or another high-risk road, follow the relevant road-safety guidance and move to a place of safety if it is possible to do so safely.
If there is an immediate danger to life, contact the emergency services.
When Do You Need Roadside Assistance?

The engine will not start
The vehicle suddenly loses power
A warning light appears alongside a serious vehicle problem
The battery is flat
You have run out of fuel
A tyre has gone flat

The vehicle has stopped after a mechanical failure
You are unsure whether it is safe to continue driving
If you are uncertain, explain the symptoms to the recovery team rather than continuing to drive a vehicle that may be unsafe.
Roadside Assistance or Vehicle Recovery?
These terms are often used together, but they can involve different levels of support.
Roadside assistance is generally focused on helping with a vehicle problem at or near the place where the vehicle has stopped.
Vehicle recovery may be required when the vehicle cannot safely continue and needs to be moved to another location.

For example, a flat battery may be dealt with through roadside battery assistance. However, if the vehicle has a serious mechanical fault and cannot safely continue, transportation or recovery may be more appropriate.
A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides both roadside recovery and vehicle transportation, allowing the next step to be considered based on the vehicle's condition and situation.

Car Won't Start

What happened

Whether you have passengers with you

If you do not know the exact cause of the problem, do not worry. Simply describe what happened before the vehicle stopped.
Roadside Assistance at Home, Work or on the Road
A vehicle does not have to break down on a major road for roadside assistance to be useful.
You may need help:

At your workplace

blocks.text: Vehicle Transport Birmingham – Safe Car & Vehicle Transportation
Need Vehicle Transport in Birmingham?

Sometimes a vehicle needs to be moved even when it is not involved in an emergency breakdown. You may need to transport a non-running car to a garage, move a vehicle after a fault, collect a vehicle from another location or take a car somewhere it cannot safely be driven.

A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides vehicle transport in Birmingham for cars and vehicles that need safe movement between locations. Our team can discuss your vehicle, collection point, destination and reason for transport before arranging the appropriate transportation support.
If your vehicle has broken down or cannot be driven safely, tell us what has happened when you call so we can determine whether vehicle recovery or transportation is the appropriate option.
What Is Vehicle Transportation?
Vehicle transportation is the process of moving a car or other vehicle from one location to another without relying on the vehicle to complete the journey itself.
This can be useful when a vehicle:
Is not running
Has suffered a mechanical fault
Is not safe to drive
Needs to go to a garage
Needs moving after an accident
Needs to be collected from another location
Needs transporting to a home address
Needs moving between agreed locations
Has been purchased and needs collection
Requires transportation as part of a recovery service
The exact transportation arrangements depend on the vehicle, its condition, location and destination.
When Might You Need Car Transport in Birmingham?
Vehicle transportation is not only for emergency breakdowns.
You may need a car transported when:
Your Car Will Not Start
A non-running vehicle may need to be moved to a garage or another suitable destination rather than driven.
Your Vehicle Has a Mechanical Fault
If a fault means the vehicle should not be driven, transportation can provide an alternative way of moving it.
Your Car Needs to Go to a Garage
You may already know which garage is going to inspect or repair your vehicle. Transportation can help move the car from its current location to the garage.
Your Vehicle Is Damaged
Following an accident or other incident, a vehicle may not be suitable for driving. In these situations, transportation or recovery may be required.
You Need to Move a Vehicle Between Locations
A vehicle may need to be moved from a home, workplace, car park, storage location or another accessible address.
Vehicle Transport After a Breakdown
A breakdown does not always mean the vehicle can be repaired at the roadside.
If your vehicle has stopped because of a mechanical, electrical or other fault and cannot safely continue, it may need to be transported to another location.

A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides both breakdown recovery and vehicle transportation, allowing customers to discuss the next step based on the vehicle's condition. The existing A.A.D service information confirms vehicle transportation as one of its core services.
For example, a vehicle may need to be moved:
Roadside → Garage
Home → Garage
Accident location → Suitable destination
Collection point → Agreed destination
Car Transport to a Garage in Birmingham
Taking a vehicle to a garage is one of the most common reasons for transportation.
You may need your car moved because:
It will not start
The engine has developed a fault
The vehicle has warning lights or mechanical problems
The car has accident damage
The vehicle has a flat battery and another underlying issue
You do not consider the vehicle safe to drive
The garage is too far to drive the vehicle safely
The vehicle needs further inspection
If you already have a preferred garage, provide the garage's location when you contact us. This allows the transportation requirements and destination to be discussed before the vehicle is moved.
Non-Running Vehicle Transport Birmingham
A non-running vehicle cannot simply be driven to its destination.
It may have:
Engine problems
Electrical faults
Battery problems
Transmission issues
Accident damage
Wheel or tyre problems
Starting problems
Other mechanical faults
If the vehicle cannot move under its own power, explain this when you contact A.A.D Transport & Recovery.
The condition of the vehicle is important because the transportation arrangements need to take into account whether it can start, move and be safely handled.
Vehicle Transport After an Accident
An accident can leave a vehicle damaged even when the driver is not sure how serious the damage is.
If your vehicle has been involved in an accident:
Prioritise everyone's safety.
Move away from immediate traffic danger where possible.
Do not drive a vehicle that appears unsafe.
Contact the appropriate emergency services if required.
Once the situation is safe, arrange recovery or transportation if the vehicle cannot continue.
A.A.D Transport & Recovery also provides accident recovery, so vehicle transportation can be considered when a damaged vehicle needs to be moved to a suitable destination.
Planned Vehicle Transportation
Not every vehicle movement is an emergency.
You may need planned transportation when:
A vehicle needs moving to a garage
A non-running car needs relocating
A vehicle needs collecting from another location
A car needs moving between properties
A vehicle cannot legally or safely be driven for the required journey
A vehicle needs transportation following a previous breakdown
When arranging planned vehicle transportation, provide the collection location, destination, vehicle type and condition in advance.
Vehicle Collection and Delivery
If a vehicle needs to be collected from one location and delivered somewhere else, the collection and destination details should be clear before transportation is arranged.
Useful information includes:
Collection address
Delivery address
Vehicle make and model
Vehicle registration
Whether the vehicle starts
Whether the vehicle can roll or move
Any visible damage
Reason for transportation
Preferred timing, where applicable
Providing accurate information helps the team understand the transportation requirements before arranging the service.
Can a Broken-Down Car Be Transported?
Yes. A broken-down car may need transportation when it cannot safely continue its journey or requires movement to a garage or another location.
The appropriate option depends on the vehicle's condition and the circumstances of the breakdown.
For example, a vehicle that has simply stopped running may require a different transportation approach from a vehicle that has significant accident damage.
A.A.D Transport & Recovery can discuss the vehicle's condition and transportation requirements when you make contact.
Where Can a Vehicle Be Transported From?
Vehicle transportation may be required from different locations across Birmingham, including:
Residential properties
Driveways
Workplaces
Garages
Car parks
Local roads
Breakdown locations
Accident locations
Private premises
Other accessible collection points
When contacting us, provide the exact collection location and destination so availability can be discussed.
Vehicle Transport Across Birmingham
A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides vehicle transportation support across Birmingham and surrounding areas.
Whether you need to move a non-running car after a breakdown, take a damaged vehicle to a garage or arrange another vehicle movement, contact the team with the collection and destination details.
If you are unsure whether your exact location is covered, provide the address when you contact us so availability can be confirmed.
What Information Do We Need?
Before arranging vehicle transportation, it helps to have the following information available:
Vehicle Details
Provide the make, model and registration of the vehicle.
Vehicle Condition
Tell us whether the vehicle starts, runs and can move.
Collection Location
Give the exact location where the vehicle needs to be collected.
Destination
Tell us where you need the vehicle transported.
Reason for Transport
Explain whether the vehicle has broken down, is damaged, needs a garage visit or needs moving for another reason.
Access Information
If the vehicle is located in a tight driveway, car park or restricted area, mention this when calling.
What If My Vehicle Cannot Move?
Tell us if the vehicle cannot start, roll or move.
A vehicle that cannot move under its own power may require additional recovery arrangements. The transportation plan should take the vehicle's condition and collection location into account.
Do not attempt to move a heavily damaged or unsafe vehicle yourself simply to make transportation easier.
Vehicle Transportation vs Breakdown Recovery
Although these services are closely connected, they are not always used for the same reason.
Breakdown recovery generally starts when a vehicle has stopped because of a breakdown or roadside problem and needs assistance.
Vehicle transportation focuses on moving a vehicle from one location to another, whether the reason is a breakdown, garage visit, planned relocation or another transportation requirement.
A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides both services, allowing customers to discuss their particular situation and determine the appropriate support.
24/7 Vehicle Recovery and Transport Support
Vehicle problems can happen at any time, and a non-running vehicle may need to be moved outside normal working hours.
A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides 24/7 breakdown and recovery support in Birmingham. Vehicle transportation is also listed as one of the company's core services.
If you need a vehicle transported, contact the team with your vehicle details, collection location and destination so your requirements can be discussed.
How Our Vehicle Transport Service Works
1. Contact A.A.D Transport & Recovery
Tell us that you need vehicle transportation and explain why the vehicle needs to be moved.
2. Provide the Collection Location
Give the exact location of the vehicle.
3. Explain the Vehicle Condition
Tell us whether the vehicle starts, runs and can move.
4. Provide the Destination
Give the garage, home address or other agreed destination.
5. Discuss the Transportation Requirements
The team can review the information and discuss the appropriate transportation support.
6. Vehicle Transportation
Once the arrangements are agreed, the vehicle can be transported to the agreed destination where the service is available.
Why Choose A.A.D Transport & Recovery?
A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides vehicle transportation alongside breakdown recovery and vehicle assessment services in Birmingham.
Customers can contact the team for:
Vehicle transportation
Breakdown recovery
Roadside recovery
Vehicle assessment
Accident recovery
Support for non-running vehicles
Birmingham and surrounding area coverage
Free quotes
The aim is to make vehicle transportation straightforward, with clear communication about the vehicle, collection point and destination.
Need Vehicle Transport in Birmingham?
Whether your vehicle has broken down, needs taking to a garage or simply needs moving from one location to another, A.A.D Transport & Recovery can discuss your transportation requirements.
Provide your vehicle details, collection location and destination when you call.
Free quotes available.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is vehicle transportation?

Vehicle transportation is the process of moving a car or other vehicle from one location to another. It can be used for non-running vehicles, garage transfers, damaged vehicles, planned vehicle movements and other situations where driving the vehicle is not suitable.
Do you provide vehicle transport in Birmingham?
Yes. A.A.D Transport & Recovery lists vehicle transportation as one of its core services and provides breakdown and recovery support across Birmingham and surrounding areas.
Can you transport a non-running car?
A non-running vehicle may require transportation because it cannot complete the journey under its own power. Tell the team whether the vehicle starts, runs or can move when arranging the service.
Can you transport my car to a garage?
Yes. Vehicle transportation can be used to move a car to a garage or another agreed destination. Provide the vehicle's current location and the garage destination when contacting the team.
Can you transport a damaged vehicle?

A damaged vehicle may require transportation if it is not safe or suitable to drive. Explain the condition of the vehicle and any visible damage so the appropriate recovery or transportation requirements can be discussed.
Can you collect a vehicle from one location and take it somewhere else?
Vehicle transportation can be used for collection and movement between agreed locations. Provide both the collection address and destination when requesting a quote.
Can you transport a vehicle after a breakdown?

Yes. If a vehicle cannot be repaired at the roadside or is not safe to drive, vehicle transportation may be required. A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides both breakdown recovery and vehicle transportation.
What information do you need for vehicle transportation?
Useful information includes the vehicle make and model, registration, collection location, destination, vehicle condition and reason for transportation.
Can you transport a car that does not start?

A car that does not start may still be transportable, but the team needs to know its condition before arranging the service. Tell us whether the vehicle can move, roll or steer and explain any damage or mechanical problem.
How much does vehicle transport cost in Birmingham?

The price can depend on factors such as the collection location, destination, vehicle condition and transportation requirements. Contact A.A.D Transport & Recovery for a quote based on your specific journey.
Do you provide vehicle transport 24/7?
A.A.D Transport & Recovery provides 24/7 breakdown and recovery support. Contact the team to discuss your vehicle transportation requirements and availability.
